messages:
lia: Heads up — after the 23:00 deploy we started seeing sporadic SCIM deprovisions from Okta. Looks like entityID canonicalization changed on the IdP side and a few RBAC mappings failed.
kevin: I'm seeing repeated errors in the scim-provisioner logs: `403` followed by a KMS decrypt error. Example from prod logs:
```
2026-03-22T23:12:05Z scim-provisioner ERROR externalId lookup failed: kms:decrypt failed: context mismatch for alias 'customer:rekey-2026'
```
ana: What exactly did the 23:00 patch change? @matt did we flip any metadata normalization flags? :thinking:
matt: We enabled strict entityID normalization (strip trailing slash, lowercase host) in the SAML middleware to reduce duplicate SP entries. Didn't expect Okta to send mixed formats for the same app. I can roll a mapping but need quick confirmation on impact.
lia: Audit shows SAML assertions were accepted but NameID and entityID fields differ between sessions. RBAC lookup uses canonical entityID -> mismatch -> fallback created new service account which then triggered SCIM backfill. Forensic snippet:
```
assertion.subject.nameid = 'user@example.com'
assertion.issuer.entityId = 'https://okta.company.com/app/12345/'  # trailing slash variant
rbac.mapping.key = 'https://okta.company.com/app/12345'  # canonical no-slash
```
kevin: SCIM then tried to decrypt the stored envelope for the legacy svc acc and KMS rejected because alias rotated to 'customer:rekey-2026' and the context we compute for unwrap didn't match the envelope. KMS audit shows a few `DecryptDenied` events with context mismatch.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy 17788 -> staging succeeded :white_check_mark:
nana: Immediate plan proposal: 1) Add back-compat entityID mapping in the IdP connector, 2) add temporary alias allowance in kms-unwrap to accept legacy alias for 24h, 3) run idempotent SCIM backfill job, 4) open vuln-triage for KMS alias handling. Thoughts?
lia: Sounds good. I'll open an incident with notes and assign tasks: kevin -> KMS temporary fix + audit, matt -> IdP mapping + canary, ana -> SCIM backfill script. ETA 2h for mitigation.
kevin: Quick patch I can push now to allow legacy alias in unwrap: `kms.unwrap(envelope, allowed_aliases=['customer:rekey-2026','customer:default'])` — this short-circuits the strict alias check for 24h while we backfill. Will add audit flags to log any usage.
matt: I'll add the mapping in identity-config: map both variants to the same SP id, then roll canary to 5% in us-west. @ops-bot please pause canary if scim errors > 5%.
ops-bot: canary started -> 5% traffic mapped -> error rate dropped from 4.7% to 0.8%
lia: Nice. Action items: export audit logs for the window 2026-03-22T22:50:00Z -> 2026-03-22T23:30:00Z and push to sec-s3 bucket for postmortem. Also add automated test cases for entityID normalization to the onboarding suite.
nana: For SCIM backfill: we'll re-run the job with `--allow-legacy-extid` and `--dry-run` first, then safe-retry. Add idempotency checks to avoid double deprovisioning.
kevin: I'll follow up tomorrow with a postmortem on whether alias rotation exposed any surface for key material leakage. Initial audit shows only `DecryptDenied` (no successful unauthorized unwraps).
lia: Good. I'll create the incident ticket and link to this thread. Thanks everyone — please post updates in the incident channel once fixes are live. :thumbsup:
